published_statement: Coc et al. 2007 eq. (13) (as READ by the sibling audit): 'Lambda = mu (m_c m_b m_t / mu^3)^(2/27) exp(-2 pi/(9 alpha_s(mu)))' 'for mu > m_t up to some unification scale in the standard model'; eq. (14): 'Delta Lambda/Lambda = R Delta alpha/alpha + (2/27)(3 Delta v/v + Delta h_c/h_c + Delta h_b/h_b + Delta h_t/h_t)'; footnote 1: 'In supersymmetric models, additional thresholds related to squark and gluino masses would affect this relation.' b_0(n_f) = 11 - 2n_f/3 (Gross-Wilczek/Politzer 1973, restated Hill-Solon eq. 109). With Delta alpha = Delta h = 0 this is exactly the tree's Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27) and d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9.
published_hypotheses: One-loop running: 1/alpha_s(mu) = (b_0/2 pi) ln(mu/Lambda), b_0(n_f) = 11 - 2n_f/3 (SU(3), n_f Dirac quarks in the fundamental); no b_1 or higher
Leading-order decoupling: alpha_s continuous at each heavy threshold mu = m_Q (exact at one loop in MSbar only at mu = m_Q; at other mu the one-loop decoupling log ln(mu^2/m^2)/(6 pi) applies)
Scale mu between m_t and 'some unification scale'; Standard-Model coloured content in that interval (footnote 1: extra coloured thresholds change the relation)
Heavy-quark masses m_Q = h_Q v; the variation split into Delta h_Q and Delta v
High-scale coupling variation tied to Delta alpha by a GUT-dependent R (R-term zero when alpha_s is held fixed at the high scale, the tree's H1)
Light quarks u, d, s below every heavy threshold (n_f = 3 theory at hadronic scales)

rederivation.outcome: 0 failures, exit 0 (python3, ~25 s). (1) From explicit Gell-Mann matrices: Tr(T^aT^b) = delta/2, f^acd f^bcd = 3 delta, sum T^aT^a = 4/3 -- so (11/3)C_A - (4/3)T_F n_f = 11 - 2n_f/3; Nielsen-Hughes spin formula reproduces 11 and -2/3; step b_0(n-1) - b_0(n) = 2/3 for all n; b_0 > 0 iff n_f <= 16. (2) sympy chain with alpha_s continuous at mu = m_Q: Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27), dimension closes (7/9 + 6/27 = 1), d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9; each exponent telescopes to (2/3)/b_0(3). address.py's beta0, _lambda_exponent_direct, dln_lambda_dln_v and dln_mp_dln_v('H1') imported read-only and agree exactly. (3) At one loop, matching at mu = kappa m_Q leaves 2/9 unchanged and kappa only rescales Lambda_3 by a v-independent constant; the one-loop decoupling log 1/(6 pi) equals (b_lo - b_hi)/(4 pi). (4) INDEPENDENT beyond-LO route: numerical RG with alpha_s(mu0 = 1 TeV) and m_Q(mu0) proportional to v held fixed, thresholds found at m_Q(m_Q), Lambda_3 read as the scale where alpha_s^(3) reaches 0.35 (and 0.5, agreeing to 1e-10, as massless n_f = 3 requires): LO 0.222222 (reproduces the tree), NLO 0.23006 (+3.5%), NNLO 0.23501 (+5.8%); alpha_s(M_Z) +- 0.0009 moves NNLO by < 0.1%. (5) Per quark at NNLO vs Hill-Solon N3LO (sibling's transcription): top 0.07595 vs 0.07567 (+0.4%), bottom 0.07861 vs 0.07899 (-0.5%), charm 0.08045 vs 0.08373 (-3.9%) -- the charm leg carries the spread, matching Hill-Solon's 'poorly convergent alpha_s(m_c) expansion'; recorded as a truncation spread between two routes, not an error in either. NLO differs more (+3.5% vs +6.8%) because resummed running and expansion at alpha(m_Q) differ at that order.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors used: b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 (1973) is group theory times a one-loop coefficient -- it uses no measured datum, and nothing measured since (alpha_s, quark masses, the absence of new coloured states at the LHC) can move it; C_A = 3, T_F = 1/2 are recomputed here exactly. The one-loop threshold chain (Coc et al. 2007) likewise uses no datum: 7/9 and 2/27 are ratios of b_0's. What they did not use was higher-order QCD, and that was a choice, not missing data -- two-loop running and the O(alpha_s^3) decoupling constants (CKS 1997) existed in 2007. What came later: the O(alpha_s^3) heavy-quark matrix elements (Hill-Solon 2014) and the current alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1180(9). Does having them change the conclusion? The number, yes, by a computed +5.8% (NNLO, numerical RG here) to +7.3% (N3LO, Hill-Solon): d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 0.235 .. 0.238, not 2/9 'EXACTLY'. The conclusions resting on it (K_mu O(1) and negative; order-of-magnitude densities), no. Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: the one-loop value is data-free and reproduced exactly by two routes; the refinements are stable (< 0.1% over the alpha_s band). Evidence for it in its weak form: the only datum that could genuinely move the one-loop sum is the particle content between m_t and the high scale, which is an assumption about unmeasured physics, not a measured value -- the tree drops it silently.
grade_evidence: The computation is right as a one-loop statement: b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 recomputed from explicit SU(3) generators (C_A = 3, T_F = 1/2); the chain Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27) and d ln Lambda_3/d ln v = 2/9 re-derived in sympy, identical to address.py's own functions (imported read-only) and to Coc et al. eq. (13) (READ in this docket by the sibling audit); robust at one loop to the matching point (any fixed kappa). But the tree uses it as the physical derivative, 'EXACTLY' (address.py:97, 498-500, 506-507, 528-531, 769-770; excite.py:164-165, 1400-1401, 1540), keeping 'one-loop' only at address.py:88. Beyond one loop, computed here by an independent numerical-RG route, it is 0.23006 (NLO) and 0.23501 (NNLO), and 0.23839 by Hill-Solon's N3LO closed form; top and bottom legs agree between routes to 0.5%, the charm leg spreads 3.9%. The SM-coloured-content scope (Coc footnote 1) is also dropped. Not WRONG: no counterexample; 2/9 is the correct one-loop value and the tree lists the Yukawa-running correction as OPEN (excite.py:285). Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum enters the one-loop value, and the beyond-LO shift is stable to < 0.1% over alpha_s(M_Z) +- 0.0009. Not STANDS: 'exactly' is claimed on a larger class (the physical derivative) than the one-loop class on which it holds. SOURCE LIMIT, stated: no PDF was opened in this stage (alphaXiv quota exhausted, arXiv 403); the published statement rests on the sibling audit's in-docket READ of Coc et al. and Hill-Solon, and Gross-Wilczek/Politzer are NAMED-NOT-READ. The re-derivation half of the grade is independent of that limit. Consistent with sibling audits dlnlambdaqcd-dlnv-2-9 and svz-1978 (both NARROWED on the same leading-order qualifier).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owners carry 'one loop, alpha_s continuous at m_Q, SM coloured content between m_t and the high scale' wherever 2/9 is consumed (address.py:97, 498-500, 528, 769; excite.py:164-165, 1400, 1540), or quote the beyond-LO 0.235 .. 0.238. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a coloured BSM state between m_t and the high scale (with or without v-dependent mass) would move the one-loop sum; so would a downstream use sensitive to the few-per-cent shift. To WRONG: a consuming conclusion that needs 2/9 to better than ~5% (none found).
